description: Harden the internal/git command layer against git argument/option injection. All git subprocess calls live in internal/git/git.go and pass arguments positionally with no shell, so the real vulnerability is that user-supplied ref names beginning with '-' (or containing ref metacharacters) can be interpreted by git as OPTIONS. Add strict validation for user-supplied ref names and add end-of-options / '--' guards before positional ref and commit arguments so untrusted values can never be parsed as flags. This feature touches ONLY internal/git and its tests; the UI already surfaces returned errors to the user via m.err.
steps: Create internal/git/validate.go with an exported ValidateRefName(name string) error. It must reject: empty/whitespace-only names; any name whose first non-space rune is '-' (option-injection guard); names containing whitespace or ASCII control characters; and names violating git ref rules (contains any of the sequence '..', the characters space, '~', '^', ':', '?', '*', '[', '\\', the sequence '@{', a component starting with '.', a '.lock' suffix, or leading/trailing '/'). Return descriptive errors, e.g. fmt.Errorf("invalid ref name %q: must not start with '-'", name). Keep it a pure function (no exec) so it is fast and unit-testable.

In git.go, call ValidateRefName at the top of the functions that accept user-typed names and return its error early: CreateBranch(name) (before the existing empty check, so validation replaces/augments it), RenameBranch(newName), CreateBranchAt(name), and CreateTag(name). Do NOT validate values that come only from git's own output (branch/tag/stash lists) with ValidateRefName if that would reject legitimate existing refs; instead protect those call sites with the end-of-options guard in the next step.

Add option-injection guards to positional ref/commit arguments in git.go by inserting a '--end-of-options' token immediately before the untrusted positional argument(s), keeping all real option flags BEFORE it (verified: 'git show --stat -p --end-of-options <hash>' is accepted, but option flags placed AFTER --end-of-options are rejected). Apply to at least: SwitchBranch ('git checkout --end-of-options <name>'), GetCommitDetail ('git show --color=always --stat -p --end-of-options <hash>'), ShowTag (same as GetCommitDetail), DeleteBranch ('git branch <flag> --end-of-options <name>'), RenameBranch ('git branch -m --end-of-options <old> <new>'), CreateBranch non-checkout ('git branch --end-of-options <name>') and checkout ('git checkout -b --end-of-options <name>'), CreateBranchAt ('git branch --end-of-options <name> <ref>'), CreateTag (place --end-of-options before <name>/<ref> while keeping -a/-m before it), DeleteTag ('git tag -d --end-of-options <name>'), PushTag ('git push --end-of-options <remote> <name>'), DeleteRemoteTag ('git push <remote> --delete --end-of-options <name>' - keep --delete before the guard), StashPop/StashApply/StashDrop/StashShow (insert --end-of-options before <ref>), and GetDiffBetween (pass base and target as two separate positional args guarded by --end-of-options instead of concatenating 'base..target', i.e. 'git diff --color=always --stat -p --end-of-options <base> <target>').

Manually verify each rewritten command still works by running the existing internal/git test suite; if any git version rejects --end-of-options for a specific subcommand during testing, fall back to a leading '--' separator or a validated positional arg for that one command and note it in findings.

Create internal/git/validate_test.go with table-driven tests for ValidateRefName covering valid names (feat/x, v1.0.0, release-2, feature/login) and invalid names ("", "  ", "-D", "--force", "has space", "a..b", "a~b", "a^b", "a:b", "a?b", "a*b", "a[b", "tip@{0}", ".hidden", "foo.lock", "/lead", "trail/"). Assert error for each invalid case and nil for each valid case.

Add tests (in validate_test.go or git_ext_test.go, reusing setupRepo from tag_test.go) proving the guards: CreateBranch("-D", true), RenameBranch(existingBranch, "--force"), CreateBranchAt("-x", <ref>), and CreateTag("-d", "", "") each return a non-nil error AND do not create/modify any ref (verify via GetBranches / GetTags). Keep the existing TestBranchLifecycle, TestGetRefs, TestGetDiffBetween, TestTagLifecycle, TestGetReflogAndRecover passing unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: ValidateRefName rejects empty, leading-dash, whitespace, control-char, and git-ref-metacharacter names and accepts ordinary branch/tag names; covered by validate_test.go.
CreateBranch, RenameBranch, CreateBranchAt, and CreateTag return an error (and make no repo change) when given a name starting with '-'.
Every git.go function that passes a user- or list-derived ref/commit positionally uses a '--end-of-options' (or '--') guard so the value cannot be parsed as an option.
All pre-existing internal/git tests still pass unchanged.
go build ./..., go vet ./..., and go test ./... all pass.
verification: go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...
findings: Added internal/git/validate.go with pure-Go ValidateRefName (no exec): rejects empty/whitespace-only, leading '-' (option-injection guard, checked on first non-space rune), whitespace/control chars, and git ref metacharacters ('..', '~', '^', ':', '?', '*', '[', '\\', '@{'), any path component starting with '.', '.lock' suffix, and leading/trailing '/'. Called ValidateRefName early in CreateBranch, RenameBranch(newName), CreateBranchAt(name), CreateTag(name); it replaces the old empty-string checks. Added '--end-of-options' guards before untrusted positional args in: GetCommitDetail, SwitchBranch, DeleteBranch, RenameBranch (git branch -m --end-of-options old new), CreateBranch non-checkout (git branch --end-of-options name), CreateBranchAt (git branch --end-of-options name ref), CreateTag (git tag [-a -m msg] --end-of-options name [ref]), DeleteTag, ShowTag, PushTag, DeleteRemoteTag (--delete kept before guard), StashPop/StashApply/StashDrop/StashShow, and GetDiffBetween (now passes base and target as two separate positional args after --end-of-options instead of concatenating 'base..target'). DEVIATION: 'git checkout -b --end-of-options <name>' does NOT work because '-b' consumes the very next token as the new branch name, so --end-of-options became the branch name and TestBranchLifecycle failed. Fallback per plan: CreateBranch checkout path uses 'git checkout -b <name>' with the name relying on the already-run ValidateRefName (which forbids leading '-'), documented via a code comment. All other subcommands accepted --end-of-options fine. Added internal/git/validate_test.go: table-driven TestValidateRefName (valid: feat/x, v1.0.0, release-2, feature/login, main; invalid list per spec) and TestRefGuardsRejectOptionInjection proving CreateBranch("-D",true), RenameBranch(existing,"--force"), CreateBranchAt("-x",ref), CreateTag("-d","","") all error and leave branch/tag sets unchanged (reuses setupRepo + contains helpers). Verified: go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./... all pass; existing tests unchanged and green. REVIEW-FIX PASS (2026-07-10): (1) Strengthened TestRefGuardsRejectOptionInjection so it now actually exercises the ValidateRefName calls. Previously it passed even when ValidateRefName was stubbed to `return nil`, because git independently rejects dash-leading names once they land as positionals after --end-of-options. Fix: the test now routes 8 names (dash names -D/--force/-x/-d PLUS ref-metacharacter names a..b/foo.lock/.hidden/trail/ that git would reject with its OWN differently-worded message) through all five validated command entry points (CreateBranch checkout+no-checkout, RenameBranch, CreateBranchAt, CreateTag) and asserts each error contains ValidateRefName's distinctive text "invalid ref name". Verified meaningful: stubbing ValidateRefName to `return nil` makes the test FAIL (git's messages say "is not a valid branch/tag name", not "invalid ref name"); restoring it passes. Still asserts no branch/tag created/modified. (2) Guard consistency: DeleteRemoteTag now emits 'git push --delete --end-of-options <remote> <name>' (was 'git push <remote> --delete --end-of-options <name>'), guarding BOTH remote and name like PushTag, while keeping --delete before the guard so git still parses it as an option. Verified in a scratch repo with a bare remote: 'git push --delete --end-of-options origin <tag>' deletes correctly, whereas 'git push --end-of-options origin --delete <tag>' fails ('src refspec --delete does not match any') because --delete becomes a positional after the guard. Behavior for the hardcoded "origin" default is preserved. NOTE (no code change needed): the tag.go 'P' remote-delete confirmation still has no unit test because the repo has no Bubble Tea UI test harness, consistent with the rest of the codebase.
